steps: Unpack & inspect
Do any fuel conversion and firebox panel kit while the stove is still on the pallet. Open the firebox with the latch tool and check the hardware bag.

Enamel parts damage easily and the stove is heavy: don't drag it by the legs, and get help moving it.

  1. Open the front door (it swings open to the left).
  2. Lift off the top plate grills and top plate. Re-install the top plate before connecting the vent.
  3. Use the latch tool from the pallet to pull the two latch hooks off the glass frame; tilt the frame forward and lift it off.
  4. Check the hardware bag: LP Conversion Kit 158295, rock wool embers (1 oz.), 3 door adjustment washers, manual 130112, 2 top plate grills. Report missing items to the dealer.
Location & clearances
Rear 2", side 7 3/8", corner 3 3/8", ceiling 33 1/2" to combustibles. Check alcove and mantel limits and floor protection (never directly on carpet, vinyl or linoleum).
Vent system & restrictor
Top plate on first. Use one approved vent maker's parts, seal inner-pipe joints (no silicone) and set the exhaust restrictor for the termination zone.

The exhaust restrictor plate sits in the firebox exhaust outlet. It prevents overly strong draft that can cause poor combustion and a weak flame picture. The dial runs from the factory-set fully open position to about 70% restriction; lettered positions A–D match the termination zones of the vent matrix (Fig. 6.2, a diagram).

  1. Loosen the lock nut with a 10 mm open-end wrench.
  2. Use the pivot tab to set the dial to the position for the termination zone.
  3. Re-tighten the lock nut.

On a division line, use the less restrictive position (manual example: 10 feet high, offset 7 feet = Position B). Co-linear installs of any height: Restriction A; B if the flame is overactive; C and D not advised.

Joints: a 1/8" bead of high-temperature sealant or Mil-Pac on the male section of the inner vent pipe. Never modify venting or use damaged parts; never connect to a chimney serving another appliance.
Termination limits
Max 35 ft total and 20 ft horizontal; a horizontal termination needs a 24" minimum vertical rise. Keep the cap inside the matrix zones and the exterior clearances (Fig. 6.11).
Fuel conversion (if LP)
An authorized technician fits kit 158295: burner and pilot injectors, LP shutter lock screw, upper baffle wings, regulator tower and labels.

1. Turn off the gas. Open the door, release the glass frame latches, tilt the frame forward and lift it out.
  2. Open the controls compartment; loosen the air shutter wing nut below the firebox floor and push the stem fully back.
  3. Lift the front of the burner off its support brackets, pull it forward off the injector and out through the door.
  4. Change the burner injector (1/2" open-end wrench or deep-well socket). Don't over-tighten: it can damage the brass elbow and leak.
  5. LP only: install the 1/2" air shutter lock screw.
  6. Pilot: remove the pilot shield (1/4" nut driver), pull off the pilot hood, swap the pilot injector (4mm hex key), refit hood and shield.
  7. LP only: remove two 10 mm nuts to drop the exhaust baffle; loosen the two 10 mm nuts on the upper baffle, break off both end wings, retighten; replace the lower baffle.
  8. Refit the burner level and securely engaged with the front supports.
  9. Swap the regulator tower (Torx T-20).
  10. Labels: A on the lower door hinge, B on the rating plate, the small label on the valve.
  11. Reassemble, apply gas, leak-check with soapy water or a digital gas detector (never an open flame), and confirm pressures with a manometer.
Installer note (Fig. 7.3): the pilot shield is removed for propane in a minimum vent run. On taller vents or in high winds it can stay installed if nuisance outages occur. Keep the shield.
Gas supply + leak test
3/8" npt with a 1/2" diameter supply to the flex line at the rear leg, with a shut-off valve and union in the same room. Leak-test every joint.

• Route the supply to the flex line behind the utility cover at the rear leg.
  • Flexible gas appliance connectors are acceptable in many U.S. areas; Canadian methods vary with local code.
  • Follow local code, or the current National Fuel Gas Code ANSI Z223.1/NFPA 54 or CAN-B149.
  • Massachusetts: a T-handle gas cock is required (248CMR).
  • Use propane-resistant sealing compounds on propane units.
  • Turn on the gas and test all joints for leaks, never with an open flame.
Check gas pressure
Manometer on the valve test points (A manifold, B inlet) with the knob on HIGH. Isolate the stove during supply-line pressure tests.
Panels, then burner media
Fit any firebox panel kit after conversion or altitude kits. Install the chosen media last, keeping the pilot carry-over area and burner perimeter clear.

• Panel kits (Skamol 158046, black reflective 157965): rear panel behind the pilot assembly shield on the rear shelf; side panels on the side shelves, held by the retainer tabs. Fragile: support with both hands.
  • Log set 158045: base log on the two burner pins, side logs against the back corners. Ember stones in a thin layer over the rear ports only. Rock wool: small pinches over the front of the burner base, no more than 1/4 of the supply.
  • River rock 158055: engage the burner pins in the correct orientation (Figs. 12.3a/b).
  • Tumbled stones 158054: one layer; don't fully block ports or the air space at the burner skirt.
  • Fire glass (156815, 157342): no more than the four pounds supplied; keep the area in front of the pilot clear.
  • Beach Fire logset 158229: logs engage the adaptor plate pins (photos, pp. 23–24).
System check
Purge the line on first lighting. Pilot: steady, blue at the hood with traces of yellow, engulfing the top 1/8" of the thermocouple.

• From a cold start, letting the pilot burn 10 - 15 minutes to establish positive draft may help before turning the burner on.
  • Pilot flame: steady (not lifting or floating), fully engaged with the thermopile, projecting toward the burner carry-over ports.
  • Adjust it with the screw to the left of the valve regulator (Fig. 13.2): qualified technician only.
  • The more vent offsets, the greater the need for an air shutter adjustment.
  • Co-linear: on first lighting after removing the front glass, light the pilot and leave it 10-15 minutes to establish draft.

After confirming burner function at all heat levels, the owner runs the stove low for several hours, then high for several hours, to cure the paint.
Air shutter & flame picture
Start mid-range, burn 20-30 minutes on HIGH, and open the shutter in 1/16" - 1/8" steps if the flame is weak, slow or sooty. Tighten the wing nut.

Open the controls access door and loosen the wing nut. Slide the stud forward to open (more air), back to restrict.

  • Too much air: blue, transparent, "anemic" flame.
  • Too little air: very long yellow flames, black soot on the logs, firebox walls and possibly the termination cap.
  • Let the flames settle a few minutes after each adjustment.

Natural gas (conversion section, p. 17): start at 1/16" open, run at least 15 minutes, then adjust in 1/16" - 1/8" increments.

Note: p. 4 gives the factory air shutter settings as NG 0" and LP 1/16" open, but p. 17 says the NG factory setting is 1/16" open.

panels.title: Anemic or overactive flame
items: Blue, transparent ("anemic") flame → air shutter setting too large
Overly strong draft → poor combustion, weak flame picture; set the exhaust restrictor for the termination zone
Co-linear install with overactive flame → restrictor from A to B (C and D not advised)

panels.title: Long yellow flames & soot
items: Very long yellow flames, black soot on logs, firebox walls or termination cap → air setting too small
Soot = incomplete combustion and/or too little combustion air at the shutter opening
Propane on a minimum vent configuration → brush the logs, remove some or all rock wool
Weak, slow or sooty flame on HIGH → open the shutter in 1/16" - 1/8" steps

panels.title: Draft & nuisance outages
items: Poor draft or draft reversal → steep roofs, nearby trees, windy sites; a taller vent may help
Nuisance outages (propane, taller vent or high wind) → pilot shield can stay installed
Cold start → letting the pilot burn 10 - 15 minutes before the burner may help establish draft
Co-linear, first lighting after removing the glass → pilot 10-15 minutes before the burner

panels.title: Pilot won't light or stay lit
items: Pilot goes out when the knob is released → repeat lighting steps 5 through 7
Won't stay lit after several tries → knob to OFF; call a service technician or gas supplier
Knob doesn't spring back → stop; call a service technician or gas supplier
Knob won't push in or turn by hand → don't force or repair it; call a qualified technician

light.title: Lighting the stove
light.html:
You light the pilot by hand with the red spark button. The controls are in the compartment under the firebox, and these steps are also on the rating-plate lanyard there.

  1. Stop. Smell all around the stove for gas, including next to the floor, since some gas is heavier than air.
  2. Set the burner ON/OFF switch to OFF, or set the thermostat (if you use one) to its lowest setting.
  3. Make sure the shut-off valve on the gas supply line is open.
  4. Push the valve control knob in slightly and turn it clockwise to OFF. Don't force it.
  5. Wait five minutes to clear out any gas. If you then smell gas, stop and follow the gas-smell steps under Safety.
  6. Push the knob in slightly and turn it counter-clockwise to PILOT.
  7. Push the knob all the way in and hold it. Press the red spark button again and again until the pilot lights. Keep holding the knob for about one minute, then let go. It should spring back and the pilot should stay lit. If it goes out, repeat steps 5 through 7.
  8. Turn the knob counter-clockwise to ON.
  9. Set the burner switch to ON, or set the thermostat to the temperature you want.
Call your service technician or gas supplier if the knob doesn't spring back, or if the pilot won't stay lit after several tries (turn the knob to OFF first). Use only your hand on the knob, never tools. If the knob won't push in or turn by hand, don't try to repair it: call a qualified technician. Force or attempted repair may result in a fire or explosion.

off.title: Turning the stove off
off.html:
There are two ways to turn the stove off.

Everyday: burner off, pilot on

Set the burner switch to OFF. The flames go out, but the small pilot flame stays lit. That's normal.

Complete shutdown

Set the burner switch to OFF. Then push in the valve control knob and turn it clockwise to OFF. Don't force it.

Before any service work, turn off the gas supply and disconnect power from the stove.
It can be hot even when it looks off. On a thermostat, the stove may be very hot even when the burner doesn't seem to be on. With a remote, it can turn on suddenly. Keep children away.

Because the pilot can burn all the time, take care when you use household products that give off flammable vapors near the stove.

firstfire.title: Your first fires
firstfire.html:
The stove's paint is air-dried at the factory and finishes curing with heat during the first fires. That gives off some odor and visible smoke. It's normal.

Before the first fire

  • Ventilate: open doors and windows, and use a fan to move fresh air through the room.
  • Vacate: the fumes are non-toxic, but they can bother babies, small children, pregnant women, older people, pets and anyone with breathing problems.

Break it in

Once your installer has confirmed the burner works at all heat levels, run the stove on a low setting for several hours, then on a high setting for several hours.

Fog and white film on the glass

A little fog can form on the glass each time you light the stove. It clears as the glass heats up. After the first few fires, a white, powdery film appears on the inside of the glass. Clean it off once the glass is cool, or it can permanently etch the glass.

Creaks and pings

Cast iron and steel expand and contract as they heat and cool. Creaking or pinging sounds are normal.

glass.title: Cleaning the glass
glass.html:
Clean the glass only when it needs it, and never while it's hot.

  1. Wipe the glass with a clean, damp, soft cloth.
  2. Dry it with a soft towel. Take care not to scratch it.

For the white, powdery film after the first few fires, use a non-abrasive glass cleaner made for gas hearth appliances, or warm water.

Don't use abrasive cleaners or ammonia-based cleaners on the glass.

Check it once a year

  • Look for scratches. They weaken the glass, and a scratched panel should be replaced.
  • Check the gasket around the glass for wear and a tight seal.
  • Never use the stove with a glass panel removed, cracked or broken. Only a licensed or qualified service person should replace glass, using genuine Jøtul glass.
  • Don't slam or strike the glass. It can shatter if something hits it.

controls.title: Know your controls
controls.html:
The controls are in the controls compartment under the firebox, behind the control door. Make sure everyone who uses the stove knows them.

Valve control knobOFF · PILOT · ON
Red spark buttonlights the pilot
Burner switchmain burner ON / OFF

The lighting steps are on the inside back cover of the manual and on the rating-plate lanyard in the controls compartment. The rating plate also carries your stove's serial number. Write it down with your purchase date, dealer and installer.

Remote and wall thermostat

A remote (224910) and a wall thermostat (750003) are optional accessories. This manual doesn't explain how to use them. If you use a thermostat, set it to its lowest setting before lighting, and to the temperature you want afterward.

Keep the remote where children can't reach it. The stove can turn on suddenly, so keep away from the burner when you use the remote.

flame.title: What the flames should look like
flame.html:
The pilot

The pilot burns behind the burner at the back of the firebox. Its flame should be steady, not lifting or floating. It should be blue around the pilot's hood, with traces of yellow toward the outer edges.

The main flames

The air shutter under the firebox is set at the factory. It can be adjusted to suit your installation and give the flame picture you want.

  • Blue, see-through ("anemic") flames mean the air setting is too large.
  • Very long yellow flames that leave black soot on the logs, inside the stove or on the outside vent cap mean the air setting is too small.

On propane with a minimum vent setup, some soot may form. If it does, clean the logs with a soft brush and remove some or all of the rock wool from the burner.

Pilot adjustment should only be done by a qualified, professional service technician.

screen.title: Caring for the safety screens
screen.html:
The front door and both side glass panels have built-in Invisimesh safety screens. They reduce the risk of burns from the hot glass and must stay installed at all times.

Cleaning

Dust, lint and other airborne debris collect on the screens. Over time, with heat, they can change the screen's color. Clean the screens now and then:

  1. Open the front door.
  2. Clean both sides of the screen with a fine, soft-bristle brush or a vacuum attachment.
  3. Press only very gently, so you don't damage the screen.

Never run the stove with the front door open or ajar.

If a screen is damaged

Don't use the stove until it's replaced. Use only genuine Jøtul screens from an authorized Jøtul dealer (side screen 158063). A screen removed for service must go back before the stove is used.

For the front screen, the manual lists Front Replacement Screen 158062 (p. 6 and p. 34). Its parts list numbers the front screen assembly itself 225950 (p. 32), and the front-screen replacement steps on p. 30 are headed with that number.

safety.title: Safety around the stove
safety.html:
If you smell gas

  • Don't try to light any appliance. Put out any open flame and open windows.
  • Don't touch any electrical switch, and don't use any phone in your building.
  • Leave the building right away. Call your gas supplier right away from a neighbor's phone, and follow their instructions. If you can't reach them, call the fire department.

Every day

  • Hot glass causes burns. Don't touch it until it has cooled, and never let children touch it.
  • Supervise young children in the room. A child guard or an adjustable safety gate is recommended if anyone at risk lives in the house.
  • Never run the stove with the front door open or ajar, or with any glass panel or safety screen removed or damaged.
  • Keep clothing and anything flammable away from the stove. Never store or use gasoline or other flammable vapors or liquids nearby.
  • Burn only natural gas or propane, never wood, cardboard, paper, coal or other solids.
  • If any part has been under water, don't use the stove. Call a qualified service technician right away to inspect the stove and replace any part of the control system and any gas control that has been under water.
Massachusetts: a carbon monoxide detector must be installed in the same room as the stove.

service.title: Annual service & upkeep
service.html:
A qualified gas technician must inspect the stove and its vent system every year. More frequent cleaning may be needed if there's a lot of lint from carpeting or bedding.

At the yearly service

  • A qualified technician inspects and cleans the pilot assembly and burner base, and replaces any part that shows corrosion.
  • The whole vent system is inspected. If it's taken apart, it must be resealed following the vent maker's instructions.
  • The glass gasket is checked for wear and a good seal.

Between visits

  • Vacuum the valve compartment regularly to remove dust and debris, more often if you have pets.
  • Keep the control compartment and the area under the stove free of dust, and keep the air flow around the stove unblocked.
  • Use a soft brush attachment near the logs, and handle them carefully.
  • Fire-glass media can discolor over time. Soak it in a detergent bath to bring back its original finish.
Before any service work, turn off the gas supply and disconnect power from the stove.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
Jøtul North America warrants these parts to the original retail purchaser against defects in material and workmanship, from the date of purchase:

Cast iron, steel doors, surround components, firebox5 years
Burner, ceramic burner, burner treatments, firebox panels2 years
Enamel finish (peeling or fading)2 years
Gas & electrical parts (controls, plumbing, valve, blower)1 year

Not covered (examples)

  • Installation or service by anyone other than an authorized installer, service agency or gas supplier. This voids the warranty.
  • Installation that doesn't follow the manual or local and national codes.
  • Normal wear parts such as paint, gaskets and glass (unless the glass is damaged by thermal stress).
  • Unauthorized modification, use or repair, damage in transit, and travel time or loss of service.

Making a claim

Keep your dated sales receipt. Contact your nearest authorized Jøtul dealer, who processes the claim. Jøtul must hear about a possible defect within 60 days of when it was first found, or could reasonably have been found. The warranty isn't transferable.

This is a summary. The full terms, exclusions and limits are in the manual.

specInlet.html:
Natural gas5.0 – 7.0 in. WC (1.25 – 1.74 kPa)
Propane11.0 – 14.0 in. WC (3.0 – 3.48 kPa)

Measure at test point B on the front of the valve, with the valve control knob set on HIGH. The tools list calls for an external regulator for propane only.

Supply-piping tests above 1/2 psig (3.5 kPa): disconnect the stove and its main gas valve. At or below 1/2 psig: isolate it by closing its manual shut-off valve.

Floor protection

Not directly on carpeting, vinyl or linoleum. On any combustible floor other than wood, install a pad of metal, wood, ceramic tile, stone or a listed hearth pad covering the full width and depth of the stove; flooring under the pad need not be removed. The minimum pad is drawn in Fig. 5.1; parallel and corner layouts are diagrams (Figs. 5.2, 5.3).

"Fire resistant" materials and fire-rated sheet rock count as combustible.

specVent.title: Venting
specVent.html:
Vertical or horizontal termination. The cap must fall in the shaded zones of the vent matrix (Fig. 6.2, p. 10, a diagram), and the exhaust restrictor is set to that zone (positions A–D).

Vertical: max horizontal run20 ft
Vertical: min vertical termination6 ft
Vertical: total run incl. offsets35 ft max
Horizontal: max vertical / horizontal run35 ft / 20 ft
Horizontal: min vertical rise24"
At minimum vertical run5 ft max horizontal
Snorkel (14" or 36")2 ft max horizontal
Co-linear2 foot max horizontal · Restriction A
Wall cut-out / floor firestop10" X 10"
  • Elbows: up to two 45° or one 90° beyond the first; reduce horizontal run 5 ft for each additional elbow.
  • Horizontal runs level or rising 1/4 in. per foot toward the cap; never downward.
  • Cap to overhead combustible projections: 3" (2 1/2" or less), 12" (more than 2 1/2"). Not recessed into a wall or siding; vinyl siding standoff (M&G Dura-Vent #950) on vinyl siding.
  • Roof: no cap discharge opening less than 18 in. horizontally from the roof surface.
  • 14" snorkel needs 12" of vent off the stove to meet the minimum rise.

Approved systems: M&G DuraVent DirectVent Pro and GS Series, Amerivent, Secure Vent, Selkirk Metalbestos Direct Temp, Metal-Fab Sure-Seal, ExcelDirect, Pro Form, Ventis Direct Vent. One manufacturer per system. Exterior terminal clearances (Canada and U.S.) are tabulated in Fig. 6.11, p. 13.

specConv.html:

Conversion is done by an authorized service technician. LP only: fit the 1/2" air shutter lock screw (it sets the minimal shutter opening) and break the end wings off the upper baffle. Swap the regulator tower, apply labels A and B and the valve label, leak-test and confirm pressures.

High altitude: most suppliers derate gas above 2000 feet, so check with the supplier first. If the gas isn't derated, install the high-altitude kit, then fill out and apply the conversion label to the rating plate.

Note: p. 4 lists the high-altitude adjustment kits as 158296 (LP) and 158294 (NG), while p. 18 says to install high-altitude kit 158059 (propane) or 158060 (natural gas).
Note: p. 4 gives the factory air shutter settings as NG 0" and LP 1/16" open, but p. 17 says the NG factory setting is 1/16" open; p. 26 says to start any adjustment from the mid-point of the range.

specMobile.html:

conflicts.issue: High-altitude adjustment kit part numbers differ: p. 4 lists LP 158296 and NG 158294; p. 18 says Kit 158059 for propane and Kit 158060 for natural gas.

Factory air shutter setting: p. 4 lists 'Factory Air Shutter Open Settings: NG - 0" LP - 1/16"'; p. 17 says 'The factory setting for NG is 1/16" open' (start at 1/16"); p. 26 says to start adjustment at the mid-point of the range. Also shown in the step9 drawer.
Front safety screen replacement part number: 158062 on p. 6 and p. 34; 225950 on p. 30 (225950 is also the front screen assembly in the p. 32 parts list). Side screen 158063 is consistent.
conflicts.reason: Two numbering systems, not a misprint: 158062 is the Front Replacement Screen (p. 6; p. 34 'GF 160 Safety Screen Barrier Replacement' list, beside Side 158063, which p. 30 calls 'Side Safety Screen Replacement Kit 158063'); 225950 is 'Screen Assembly, Front', the component number in the p. 32 parts list (the side assembly there is 225952), and p. 30 heads the front-screen procedure with that component number. The drawer now shows both, saying what each is.

review.notes: Ignition: the cover says 'Continuous Pilot Ignition' and the lighting instructions (p. 39) describe a pilot lit by hand with a red spark-ignitor button (piezo ignitor and SIT Nova 820 valve in the p. 33 parts list); the guide describes only that procedure. Several part descriptions and the p. 33 heading say 'GF 160 DV IPI', but no IPI operation is described anywhere. No remote or wall-thermostat operating instructions (both only listed as accessories, p. 4), no electrical ratings and nothing about power outages. p. 2 mentions an 'optional blower fan' hum, but no blower is in the p. 4 accessories list, so the guide leaves it out. Diagram-only content not transcribed: dimensions (Fig. 1.1, p. 4); floor-pad size (Fig. 5.1, p. 7, figure labels read 18" with 457 mm and 475 mm); parallel/corner clearances (Figs. 5.2/5.3); mantel/ceiling clearances (Fig. 5.5, p. 8); vent matrix zones A-D (Fig. 6.2, p. 10); vent-run figures (p. 12); burner flame patterns (p. 22); Beach Fire log placement (pp. 23-24). Exterior termination clearance table (Fig. 6.11, p. 13) not transcribed: the Canada/U.S. column alignment in the extracted text is ambiguous and some metric values are inconsistent (e.g. '12 in. (46 cm)'). Page headers on pp. 8, 10, 17 and the Fig. 7.10 caption are in an offset font (headers decode to '130112_Rev 2 GF 160 DV'); no content depended on them.
